rationale_evidence.statement: Exactly one archetype has execution as its essence: CAPABILITY (I-11 verbatim: 'Knowledge does not execute. Temporal: PROCESS (has a clock, two lifecycles never conflated, work-execution progression) and PROJECTION (temporal by rebuildability, authoritative only via attestation). Persistent: KNOWLEDGE outlives its artifacts; ARTIFACTS persist as representations; PURPOSE persists by enactment.

State is fundamental: S_t=(x_1,...,x_n). An event is a state transition or external report, distinguished into DomainEvent (e_t: S_t->S_{t+1}) versus ObservationEvent. rationale_evidence.anchor: Finite representability; polyglot storage (not everything is a graph); domain/infrastructure (hexagonal) separation
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues the architecture is computable in principle: a finite knowledge state K=(V,E,R,Metadata) (a typed temporal graph plus domain state) is representable since |Entities|,|Relations|,|Events| are finite at any point in time. Depicts a graph-shaped domain sketch (Entity-hasState->State, -observedBy->Observation, -participates->Event->Proposition->{supports,causes,contradicts}->Decision->Action->Outcome) but explicitly corrects that not everything should be a graph: graphs suit relationships/provenance/dependencies/causal structure but not transactional state, large numerical arrays, time series, documents, or statistical models -- KnowledgeOS should be polyglot. Defines Storage(K) without requiring Storage=GraphDatabase (possible backends: RelationalDB, GraphDB, ObjectStore, VectorIndex, TimeSeriesDB), consistent with Hexagonal Architecture: the domain defines Meaning, infrastructure defines Representation.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Core architecture runs on a normal PC; heavy computation is optional/delegable acceleration
rationale_evidence.statement: Answers directly: yes, the core architecture (typed graph operations, relational queries, event processing, deterministic rules, many statistical calculations, provenance traversal, state-machine verification, moderate simulations) can run on a normal PC; workloads like massive embeddings, LLM inference, huge graph analytics, large Monte Carlo simulation, large-scale optimization, or enterprise-wide event histories may need larger/distributed infrastructure, but these are 'implementation-scale concerns, not contradictions in the mathematical architecture'. Concludes CoreKnowledgeOS should remain computationally lightweight, with external compute as OptionalAcceleration -- the domain layer should not know GPU, only InferenceRequest; infrastructure decides LocalCPU vs RemoteGPU. Depicts a clean architecture: Domain (Knowledge/Decision/Governance) -> Ports/Contracts -> {Local DB, Graph Store, Compute Engine (Local/Remote)}.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Critical discovery: mathematical model coherent, implementation needs additional operational contracts; three-layer architecture
rationale_evidence.statement: After 50 adversarial tests find no contradiction in the mathematical kernel, states the critical discovery: the mathematical model is coherent, but the implementation requires additional operational contracts -- 'exactly what a good formal audit should reveal'. Lists newly identified mandatory contracts: Event processing (Idempotency, Ordering, Replayability); Governance (PolicyPrecedence, PolicyBinding, AuthorityBinding); Relations (TypedRelations); Concurrency (ConcurrencyControl); Models (ModelArtifactIdentity); Provenance (AcyclicDerivation) -- explicitly 'not new conceptual primitives... constraints on implementation'. Gives a three-layer architecture: Layer 1 Mathematical kernel (Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action); Layer 2 Epistemic/semantic structures (Evidence, Identity, Meaning, Provenance, Uncertainty, Causality); Layer 3 Operational contracts (Authorization, Concurrency, Idempotency, Versioning, Replay, PolicyBinding, ModelBinding).

rationale_evidence.statement: Third major principle: explanation is not necessarily causal explanation -- the simple A->B model breaks down under feedback, global constraints, emergence, nested correlations, stochastic interdependence, and multiple interacting processes, so Hooker proposes 'dynamical interdependency' as the more general relation; example: 'API latency increased' may depend on database load, connection pool, network topology, cache state, request distribution, GC behaviour, deployment topology, external dependency, and time-of-day traffic simultaneously -- there is no useful single cause, only a dependency structure.

rationale_evidence.anchor: change is always occurring and it is the stability of process organisations or patterns that requires explanation
rationale_evidence.statement: Fourth major principle: change is the default, stability requires explanation -- Bickhard's process metaphysics reverses the classical Stability->explain Change default into Change->explain Stability/Persistence, since process identity may be based on recurring organisational patterns rather than fixed material components; consequence for KnowledgeOS: knowledge objects (e.g. ADR-123) should perhaps be treated as KnowledgeIdentity+KnowledgeLifecycle+KnowledgeTransitions where identity persists through transformation, challenging Git-style v1/v2/v3 thinking with the question 'what is the invariant pattern that makes v1, v2 and v3 instances of the same evolving thing?'

rationale_evidence.anchor: reduction and emergence are intertwined ... higher level → disposable abstraction [explicitly rejected]
rationale_evidence.statement: Seventh and eighth major principles: reduction does not mean deletion of higher-level knowledge (emergent constraints make processes well-defined while reduction identifies those processes with realizing dynamical flows, giving a bidirectional Domain-constraint <-> mechanism-realisation relationship, not higher-level=disposable-abstraction); mechanisms are not necessarily fixed components (a mechanism may reuse components in different roles, have multiple realisations, interweave with other mechanisms, or emerge from lower-level mechanisms) -- Mechanism != fixed list of components, but 'organised process under conditions that realises a function.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: mechanism and module decomposition are useful but partial; pathways may capture connections omitted by other decompositions; functional decomposition is also partial and condition-dependent
rationale_evidence.statement: Eighth/ninth major principle group: decomposition is inherently partial -- mechanism/pathway/module/function decomposition strategies are each useful but partial, so KnowledgeOS should not assume one canonical decomposition of a system (bounded-context/aggregate/service/module/workflow/mechanism/data-flow/runtime-dependency/business-capability/team-ownership are different, equally legitimate projections), giving theoretical support for multiple legitimate architecture views over one system.

rationale_evidence.anchor: prediction and understanding should not be opposed ... model-free learning can produce high-dimensional internal representations that have no obvious physical interpretation
rationale_evidence.statement: Twentieth/twenty-first major principle: data-driven (model-free/machine-learning) and model-driven knowledge are complementary rather than opposed, with a mixed strategy depending on data-richness vs domain-knowledge-richness; AI-generated pattern != explained mechanism, since model-free learning can produce internal representations with no obvious physical interpretation -- KnowledgeOS should distinguish Predictive Pattern, Mechanistic Explanation, and Causal/Dynamical Model along an explicit, non-monotonic epistemic ladder (Observation->Pattern->Correlation->Model->Mechanism->Explanation->Validated invariant), where a pattern does not necessarily become a mechanism nor a model become reality.
